summary: Iter 28 — Materials tab pricing-slider race-condition fix verified end-to-end. The original bug ('sliders glitching, not mirrored, not responsive') is FIXED: dispatching a rapid burst of input events on each of the four sliders (waste, overhead, profit, contingency), every slider's DOM `value` attribute AND the yellow %-label now snap cleanly to the LAST emitted value with no rollback/oscillation (verified for waste=20.0%, overhead=28.0%, profit=30.0%, contingency=19.0%). Optimistic localCfg renders within a single frame, debounced PATCH fires after 200ms, and the Grand Total updates accordingly. ZIP-blur regression and Save-Bid regression both pass. One side-effect bug discovered during testing — see backend_issues.minor.

minor.issue: Not a backend bug, but the shared `patchTimerRef` in PricingPanel.jsx means that if the user rapidly switches between multiple sliders within the 200 ms debounce window, the pending PATCH for the previously-dragged slider is canceled and never sent. Result: only the LAST slider that was touched gets persisted to the server. During testing, a sequential burst across all 4 sliders (~210ms per slider) resulted in only contingency_pct=19 being PATCH'd; waste/overhead/profit values reverted to their server-side originals on next render. Real-world impact is low (humans rarely drag 4 sliders in <800ms) but it can surface if a user quickly tweaks two sliders in succession. Fix: keep a per-key timer map (e.g. `patchTimerRef.current[key] = setTimeout(...)`) and an abort controller per key, so each slider has its own independent debounce/cancel pipeline.

integration_issues.issue: Earlier slider's debounced PATCH is canceled when a different slider starts being dragged within 200ms; values appear to 'snap back' to server defaults after debounce flushes. See backend_issues.minor for RCA.

action_items: (Optional / minor) Refactor PricingPanel.jsx to use a per-key debounce map: `const patchTimers = useRef({})` and `patchTimers.current[key] = setTimeout(...)`, with a matching `patchAbortRef.current[key]` AbortController. This will let users tweak multiple sliders in quick succession without losing earlier values.
critical_code_review_comments: PricingPanel.jsx L25-26: `patchTimerRef` and `patchAbortRef` are single refs shared across all 4 sliders. onSliderChange unconditionally clears the previous timer regardless of which slider's value just changed, which means changes to slider A pending in the debounce window get DROPPED if the user touches slider B within 200ms. Recommend keying both refs by `key`.
PricingPanel.jsx L138 — `{Number((localCfg || cfg)[key]).toFixed(1)}%` correctly reads optimistic localCfg first; fix verified.

PricingPanel.jsx L42-44 — Server cfg → localCfg sync via useEffect([cfg]) is good, but if a PATCH response lands WHILE the user is dragging (very unlikely with debounce but possible on slow networks), localCfg is overwritten by the now-stale server value. Consider gating: `if (!patchTimerRef.current && !patchAbortRef.current?.signal.aborted === false) setLocalCfg(cfg)`, or compare timestamps. Low priority — debounce + abort already minimize this.
PricingPanel.jsx L111 — onBlur for ZIP fires synchronous PATCH without abort/debounce; OK since ZIP changes are infrequent and blur is a discrete event.

Dashboard / dev-tooling: x-component devtools render an extra `<span>` inside `<option>` in PricingPanel L180/L189 causing a React hydration warning ('In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>'). This is a dev-only x-component injection issue, not a runtime bug; flag for the dev-tools team if it bleeds into production builds.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The primary bug from the user report (slider glitching / not mirrored) is fully resolved by the localCfg + 200ms debounce + AbortController fix in PricingPanel.jsx. The single secondary issue worth fixing later is the shared patchTimerRef/patchAbortRef across all 4 sliders — make them per-key so multi-slider quick-edits don't drop earlier PATCHes. Tests used direct `input` event dispatch via Element.prototype.value setter to bypass React's synthetic event tracking properly. ZIP onBlur PATCH still works. Save Bid V1->V2 confirmed.
rca of the issue: Reported bug RCA: range-input was controlled by server state `cfg[key]`, and every onChange fired an immediate async PATCH. Fast drags produced an out-of-order response storm; setCfg from a slow response overwrote the new value, snapping the thumb backward. FIX (verified working): introduce optimistic `localCfg` state (slider reads from `(localCfg||cfg)[key]`), schedule PATCH on a 200ms debounce, and abort any in-flight PATCH when the user keeps dragging. Burst-input test shows DOM .value == final dispatched value 100% of the time with no flicker. Secondary RCA: the single shared patchTimerRef/patchAbortRef makes the debounce pipeline cross-cancel between different slider keys — patch for an earlier slider is silently discarded when the user starts dragging a different slider within 200ms. Mitigation: use a per-key Map of timers/aborts.
